There are two contradictory versions emerging.

In the complaint filed by Sutharsan/Sudharsan, he alleged that he had made a payment of 26,89,500/- (Rupees twenty-six lakhs eighty-nine thousand five hundred only) but the appellant, Suraj, did not act as per the promise, that is, to secure a government job for the complainant, Sutharsan/Sudharsan.

Support is taken from a document dated 14.05.2021, which is a Government Order in favour of the complainant,
Sutharsan/Sudharsan.

The said Government Order required the complainant,
Sutharsan/Sudharsan, to report for duty before the Revenue Officer within ten days.
It is obvious that the complainant, Sutharsan/Sudharsan, could not have been appointed on the basis of the said fake Government Order.
Reliance is also placed by the complainant, Sutharsan/ Sudharsan, upon an SMS, which gives details of the complainants appearance in an examination which was to be held in 2021.

At the same time,
it is also alleged in the complaint that, subsequently, the payment was to be treated as an equitable mortgage for an ancestral property which was to be evaluated.
The stand and stance of the appellant, Suraj, is that 26,89,500/- (Rupees twenty-six lakhs eighty-nine thousand five hundred only) was given as a loan on different dates between 2018 and 2023.
It is submitted that the payments over a period of time reflect and support the case of the appellant, Suraj.
Even as per the public prosecutor, payments were made between 2018 to 2023.

It is submitted that payment would not have been made in 2018 for an appointment in 2021 or for Suraj vs The Inspector Of Police on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51897862/
1 appearing in an exam in 2021.

sentences.text: Payments post-2021, contradict the assertions.
Besides the complainant has changed his stance.
It is accepted on behalf of the State that there is no other criminal case pending against the appellant, Suraj.
In view of the facts of the present case, we feel that the appellant, Suraj, has made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, in the event of the appellant, Suraj, being arrested in connection with Crime/First Information Report No. 231/2023 dated 03.11.2023 registered with Police Station  Pattiveeranpatti, District  Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, for offences punishable under Sections 120B, 294(b), 406, 420 and 506(i) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, he shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial court on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
The appellant, Suraj, will join the investigation and will comply with the conditions mentioned in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
We clarify that the observations made in this order and the grant of anticipatory bail will not be construed as expression of an opinion on the merits of the case.
Recording the aforesaid, the impugned judgment is set aside and the appeal is allowed in the above terms.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
................CJI.
(SANJIV KHANNA) ..................J. (SANJAY KUMAR) NEW DELHI;
NOVEMBER 12, 2024.
